newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower as soy, corn stumble late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower as soy, corn stumble late.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a late slide from the day's highs in corn and soybeans, traders said.
"We ran it up on the strength of corn and beans," a trader said. "Beans faltered, corn showed signs of weakness and there were no (wheat) buyers."

The March contract moved in a wide 12-cents-per-bushel range with fund buying driving that month to a session high of $3.80 per bushel near midday. Support was surfacing on concern about potential damage to portions of the U.S. soft red winter wheat crop because of flooding.
There were rumblings about potential delays in the seeding the U.S. spring wheat crop due to wet weather and snow in the northern U.S. Midwest.

Stopping of deliveries underpinned the market in early dealings. There were 1.22 million bushels of wheat posted Tuesday for delivery on the March contract and Produce Grain, the marketing arm of Bunge Corp, stopped 900,000 bushels, according to the CBOT. But the CBOT registrations showed an 750,000 bushel increase, leading to ideas for more deliveries.
Wheat closed unchanged to seven cents per bushel lower, with March down two at $3.71 a bushel.
Talk circulated that the wheat market was hit by an improvement in the condition rating for the U.S. hard red winter wheat crop.
The Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service Monday said the state's wheat crop received snow and rain in February and was ready to break dormancy in mostly good to excellent condition.

Technicians early Tuesday noted first resistance in the March at $3.78. Second resistance was at $3.87. The session high for March was $3.80. First support was at $3.69 and second support was at $3.60. The session low was $3.68.

The four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Tuesday. The nine day relative strength index (RSI) in the March closed at 52 percent. The market generally considers and RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Iowa Grain and LIT America bought 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said. Rand Financial sold one milion May and E.D. and F. Man sold one million of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,000 contracts, below the 19,809 traded Monday.

In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 400 May $3.60 puts and five cents and sold 400 May $3.70 puts at 8-1/4 cents. Traders also said LIT America bought 400 July $3.60 puts at 16 cents and sold 400 July $3.30 puts at five cents.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, slightly below the 8,221 traded Monday.
